{{Quote|All I know about Rodian customs is that they are big on hunting.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="soften">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
'''Rodians''' were a [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] in the [[Tyrius system/Legends|Tyrius system]]. Highly recognizable due to characteristics in facial structure and skin pigment, Rodians were infamous for their violent culture, which sprang from the difficulties of life in the jungles of their homeworld. Though they were often relegated to the fringes of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] society as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] or criminal henchmen, Rodians were not merely simple-minded thugs. The Rodian people managed to produce artists, merchants, Jedi Masters and politicians who were found even among the upper classes of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Is it just me, or are the Rodians kind of creepy?|A mercenary|<ref name="JA" />}}
[[File:Greeata.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[Greeata Jendowanian/Legends|Greeata Jendowanian]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Rodian]]
The Rodians were [[Color/Legends|green]]-skinned [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]]<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]]. They possessed distinctive faces: large, round, multifaceted [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]; tapir-like snouts; and a pair of saucer-shaped antennae on their heads, which served to detect vibrations.<ref name="Bombad Jedi D">{{TCW|Bombad Jedi|d=1}}</ref><ref name="Databank">{{DB|species|rodian|Rodian}}</ref> Rodian skin normally had a rough, pebbly texture, except on their hands and snouts.<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> The flexible snouts augmented the Rodians' finely tuned olfactory senses, collecting and filtering the air.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Their characteristically large eyes indicated a primarily nocturnal ancestry and were capable of seeing into the infrared part of the spectrum. This allowed the Rodians to visually detect the body heat of their hidden prey emanating from within the darkness.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="Bombad Jedi D" /> Due to their love of fighting and active lifestyles, most Rodians kept in good condition, normally lean and wiry. However, some Rodians became rather obese, typically those who could hire others to fight for them, such as [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] operative [[Avaro Sookcool]] or the [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] gangster [[Reelo Baruk]].<ref name="JO" /><ref name="soften" />
Rodians normally had green skin, allowing them to blend in with the vegetation of their jungle world.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> However, variations in pigment were not uncommon, which ranged from disfiguring [[birthmark]]s to discoloration of the entire body. This was distinctive among the race and gave rise to descriptive appellations such as "[[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red]]" and "[[Jannik (Rodian)|Jannik the White]]."<ref name="A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref><ref name="Starfighter: Crossbones">''[[Star Wars: Starfighter: Crossbones]]''</ref> Another notable characteristic of the Rodians were their hands. Possessing long, dexterous, sucker-tipped fingers, this trait denoted an arboreal lifestyle, which allowed the Rodians to grip trees and rocky inclines.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> A ridge of flexible spines crested their skulls, differing in volume, length, and even color. Instead of spines, some Rodians also grew hair. This was more common among females, though some males also grew it, as exemplified by [[Evo (Rodian)|Evo]] the Blue.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="Starfighter: Crossbones" /> Females were also physically distinguished by their [[Breast/Legends|breasts]] and mammary glands.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Off-world females, however, oftentimes would shave their hair and wear loose-fitting clothing in an attempt to disguise their gender.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Some females, though, would proudly flaunt their femininity if they knew it would work to their advantage.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />[[File:Rodians_with_different_skin_colors_.png|left|thumb|Rodians with different skin colors]]<div style="float:right">[[File:RodianMale-SOC.jpg|thumb|180px|A rare blue-skinned Rodian]]</div>
Rodians exuded a pungent, musky aroma, some smelling stronger than others.<ref name="Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> This scent was an oily [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromone]] excretion that served to moisturize the skin and attract potential mates.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Most [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and [[Diollan]]s found the scent to be particularly overwhelming and likened it to the "odor of animal droppings on the bottom of your boot."<ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale" /> This was not the case with all species, however, as evidenced by the unsavory use of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo's]] pheromones; a [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] bartender by the name of [[Wuher/Legends|Wuher]] ground up Greedo's body to use in the creation of a perfect [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] liquor.<ref name="Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale" /> Many would assume that all Rodians smelled the same, however Rodians themselves could differentiate the scent.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> The scent distinguished identity, communicating to Rodians an individual's family heritage and breeding.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> One Rodian's smell from a feuding clan could send a rival clan member into a warring frenzy.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

Rodians, as other species, were subject to aging. As he grew older, [[W. Wald|Wald's]] antennae began to sag, and gray patches appeared on his snout.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref>

Rodians possessed a wide vocal range and had been known to make hooting noises.<ref name="A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale" /> [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic-speaking]] Rodians had a unique accent, due to their tendency to lisp, and their difficulty pronouncing certain syllables containing "r," "l," or "s" sounds.<ref name="soften" /><ref name="sotepg">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref><ref name="TPoB">{{LivingForce|The Price of Business}}</ref>

==Culture and history==
{{Quote|The Osarians have hired Rodians?''"<br />"''Nothing like a few mercenaries to quiet things down.|[[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]|<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Rodian_War.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rodians often engaged in clan wars.]]
Rodian culture was obsessed with violence and death, due to behaviors and practices that were ingrained since their earliest ancestry. Evolving among the dangerous [[jungle/Legends|jungles]] and [[swamp/Legends|swamps]] of their homeworld, required them to compete with vicious predators for most of their food. Some of these predators, such as [[Ghest/Legends|ghests]], could wipe out entire Rodian villages. Thanks to their [[Sentience/Legends|sapience]], they developed tools and cunning hunting tactics to survive and even cleanse areas to protect their clans. The [[hunting/Legends|hunt]] became central to their culture and the hunter had the important role of [[Protector (Rin'na)]] of the settlement.<ref name="sotepg" />

As the Rodians developed further, eventually, they drove most of the other predators on the planet to near [[extinction]]. This had several effects in their history; their densely packed jungle homeworld was ill-suited for agriculture, and for survival some became gatherers or herders. They expressed their aggressive instincts in hunting (as individuals or teams) and gladiatorial contests (in arenas); these customs gave rise to the [[Rodian Theater/Legends|Rodian drama]].<ref name="sotepg" /> 

Being on the top of the food chain had also bigger effects: the absence of danger meant expansion of the enclaves and travel. Clans came in contact with each other, more often than not leading to conflicts over territorial differences or hunting rights; Rodians started to hunt each other in various wars, and Protectors formed military armies. Clans were eliminated by rival clans or enslaved by larger neighboring clans; only then there was some respite of temporary peace.<ref name="sotepg" />

Millennia later, whole regions were dominated by a handful of large, powerful clans. The [[Chief Protector]] of the most powerful clan, the [[Soammei clan]], eventually proclaimed himself ''Inta'si'rin'na'', or [[Grand Protector/Legends|Grand Protector]] of the Rodians. However this didn't stop thirst for dominance, as other clans succeeded in power, and the title of Grand Protector shifted from clan to clan through the rest of Rodian history, with the subsequent changes in loyalties and power. Grand Protectors ruled all of Rodia as dictators.<ref name="sotepg" />

Rodians had reached their industrial age when scouts from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] arrived on the planet. They too were hunted, until a clever Grand Protector realized the advantages of contact with [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] society. The hunts were called off, and a new policy was implemented. The Grand Protector declared that the best hunters, as proven by success in various gladiatorial contests and hunts on Rodia, would be allowed to leave the planet for intergalactic hunting; in reality, this limitation was a pretense so as to not let his enemies leave the planet.<ref name="sotepg" />

The Grand Protector's Hunters' Guild, or ''[[Goa-Ato/Legends|Goa-Ato]]'' was a means for hunters to leave the planet and seek an intergalactic career; it also instituted annual awards ''[[Atiang/Legends|Atiang]]'' for the best hunters, rewarding categories such as "Best Shot," "Longest Trail," or "Most Notorious Capture."<ref name="sotepg" />

Initially possessing no [[droid/Legends|droid]] technology, Rodians were introduced to it by trading with the Republic. The first ever droid on Rodia wandered off its master, who had to "hunt" it back. Thus the Rodians realized their utility for hunter training. After experimenting with repurposing existing droids, eventually Rodians developed their own for specific [[training droid/Legends|training]] roles as prey and target droids. [[Rodian D-Tec]] was a notable droid manufacturer.<ref name="sotepg" />

===Clan system===
Since ancient times, Rodians were a tribal society. A clan was ruled by a Chief Protector, and associated with some land and/or enclave; enclaves grew later into cities, and some absorbed other smaller enclaves as they grew. Clan members were sometimes wholly dedicated to some profession, organization or criminal syndicate; notable examples were the [[Neetakka clan]], whose all members were exclusively hunters; or the [[Tonena clan]], owner of the [[Tonena Munitions Corporation]] which employed almost all of its members.<ref name="sotepg" />

In later times, clans were also political entities, and were often allies or enemies with each other; their skirmishes sometimes escalated to [[Rodian Clan Wars|planetary war]]. Affiliation was often a private matter that was not usually obvious or publicly shared; Rodians who revealed their clan risked being exposed to Rodians of enemy clans that could be present. Warfare, geography and other factors shaped the development of each clan; some weaker clans remained isolated in their ancestral lands in the jungle, and limited to older technology. Newer clans were usually small groups that split from traditional clans, often supporting radical views; as these emerged in the cities, they possessed no lands; they often chose grandiose, self-important names (cf. Neetakka = "The Ultimate Hunters") to make up for their small status and numbers.<ref name="sotepg" />

In ancient times clans were often named after a tribal hero. Usually whole regions were named after the tribes that inhabited them, although sometimes the tribes were named after the region. Following is a listing of several known clans among the hundreds that flourished on Rodia:<ref name="sotepg" />

===Rodian Theater===
{{Main|Rodian Theater/Legends}}
[[File:Rodian_pacifist.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Rodian pacifist]]
For what many would consider a vicious and bloodthirsty species, Rodians were renowned for their drama. [[Rodian Theater/Legends|Rodian Theater]] began as a simple series of staged fights, encouraged by Grand Protector [[Harido Kavila/Legends|Harido Kavila]] as a way for his people to burn off their aggression. Over time, it developed into a vibrant&mdash;albeit violent&mdash;theatrical tradition. Though not as honored a profession as hunting, each clan had at least one troupe of actors that performed clan legends. Because actors were barred from directly seeking political power at home, drama became an acceptable way for dissident elements to challenge established ideas.

===Off their homeworld===
When Rodians left the planet, they went to take their hunting culture off-world; thus they work as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]], or similar occupations.<ref name="sotepg" />

Typically, the Grand Protector allowed members of the [[Goa-Ato/Legends|Goa-Ato]] to leave the planet in order to pursue a galactic career of hunting; the [[Rodian Galactic Drama Troupe]] was a notable exception, allowing performers of [[Rodian Theater/Legends|Rodian drama]] to tour the galaxy.<ref name="sotepg" />

Of course, not all Rodians found off-world were bounty hunters or artists. Some were refugees from clan feuds who illegally left Rodia in search of asylum. Illegal emigrants and their descendants born off-world could travel the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] freely and work in a variety of professions, from peaceful merchants and technicians to arms dealers and criminal henchmen. Rodian authorities treated off-world-born Rodians as alien galactic citizens, and illegal emigrants were generally not permitted to return to Rodia (though some used forged or legitimate documents to claim off-world status).<ref name="sotepg" /> Rodian politicians, such as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]&ndash;era [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]] and [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] aide [[Dar Wac/Legends|Dar Wac]], were often seen on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

===Imperial Period===
[[File:Rodian_UM.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Rodian]]
During the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Rodians were ruled by the Grand Protector Navik the Red, of the [[Chattza clan/Legends|Chattza Clan]]. After Chattza became the planetary ruler during the [[Rodian Clan Wars]] and Navik seized its power, he tightened restrictions on emigration and built ties with [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Navik ruthlessly persecuted his rivals, sentencing the entire [[Tetsu Clan]] to death. Although some Tetsus went off-world,<ref name="sotepg" /> the genocide was not restricted to Rodia, as even Tetsu refugees offworld, such as [[Greedo the Elder]] and his family, were pursued by Chattza hunters.

Especially during the Imperial era the cities were expanded significantly, a culmination of the progress that followed the Republic membership; not only the urban sprawls gained space over the former jungle areas, but whole Clan enclaves were engulfed by the cities around them, resulting to exclusively urban Clans.

Urban and younger Rodians forgot their traditions. Provincial Rodians were generally isolated not only from each other, but also from the urban areas, which they avoid, as well as political problems and galactic affairs. Even their cousins of the same clan would avoid the dangerous jungle provinces and look down on their "backwards" relatives. Jungle Rodians were highly xenophobic and hunters would use travelers as prey. Navik kept more advanced technologies away from the provinces, such as [[Chekkoo Province|Chekkoo]], and encouraged the existing segregation between the two populations; these policies served to hinder and isolate his political enemies, as he often exiled some to the jungle. Still, thanks to [[smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], some provincial Rodians could get access to higher technology such as [[power generator/Legends|power generators]], weapons, and even vehicles.<ref name="sotepg" />

===Yuuzhan Vong invasion of the galaxy and afterwards===
The [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invaded Rodia on their march to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Galactic Core]], enslaving the population. The alien invaders planned to forge their Rodian captives into deadly warbeasts, under the direction of [[Master Shaper]] [[Taug Molou]]. He took his Rodian experimental subjects apart on a cellular level, reassembling their genetic code with bits from other creatures. This experiment resulted in the creation of the [[Vagh Rodiek]], mindless warbeasts that moved on crab-like legs with sharp half-meter long scythes of bone in place of arms. The Rodian natural head-spines were mutated into razor-sharp quills. Again, the Rodians that managed to flee Rodia found themselves refugees from persecution.

The Rodians managed to return to Rodia after the war and were represented in the [[Galactic Alliance Senate]] by [[Moog Ulur]].

==Rodians in the galaxy==
===Emigration policies===
Leaving and returning to Rodia had been a complex matter, influenced by the internal conflicts. The respective Grand Protector always wished to control who leaves and comes to Rodia and tried to limit the off-world access and influence of his rival clans. This was easier when the Rodians relied to the Republic, but then Rodian businessmen acquired ships on their own. Gradually, the policies loosened, until Navik imposed stricter rules. Off-world hunters needed to win the privilege in the Goa-Ato, and some of them were assigned directly by the Grand Protector (rivals assigned to deadly missions). However such control could not be imposed on Rodians born off-world who came with Imperial [[Identichip/Legends|ID cards]].<ref name="sotepg" />

Rodians who leave illegally (rival clan members, political enemies or illegal hunters) could only smuggle themselves away, or run the Home Fleet. They could acquire ID cards from the Galactic Empire, by legal or illegal channels, in order to travel around the galaxy; the only way to return to Rodia would be to return with fake names, or on smuggler ships, sneaking through the Home Fleet, and preferably landing on areas outside the four assigned spaceports. The risk remained for those whose Imperial ID came under suspicion in one of the spaceports.<ref name="sotepg" />

===Criminal underworld===
[[File:ProfessionalKiller-HG.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Rodian hired killer]]
Working for the highest bidders, Rodians also found work as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]].<ref name="OW guide" /> During Navik's rule, all off-world Rodian bounty hunters, criminals and mercenaries, were ordered to report to him on their employers's activities, even if it was the Galactic Empire itself, so that the Grand Protector had knowledge on the politics around the galaxy.<ref name="sotepg" />

Perhaps the most well-known, though considered by many to be a laughable disgrace, attempt made by a Rodian bounty hunter was that of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] on [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. On a contract for the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], Greedo accosted the notorious [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] in a [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], threatening to turn him in to Jabba. In somewhat confusing circumstances, Greedo was shot by the smuggler, although there is some controversy over exactly how this happened. Greedo's backup had actually been paid off by two other Rodian bounty hunters, [[Thuku]] and [[Neesh/Legends|Neesh]], who had identified him as from the rival Tetsu Clan, and wished him killed.

The strong association with the bounty hunter profession led to the formation of many armament companies on Rodia. These included the [[Salus Corporation/Legends|Salus Corporation]], [[Sancretti Arms & Munitions, Interstellar]], [[N'Gant-Zarvel]], [[Tonena Munitions Corporation]] and [[Rheshalva Interstellar Armaments/Legends|Rheshalva Interstellar Armaments]]. Ranged weapons, such as the [[N'Gant-Zarvel]] [[9118 heavy carbine]], and bladed weapons, like the [[Repulsor throwing razor/Legends|Repulsor throwing razor]] and [[Rodian razor-stick|Razor stick]], were popular items produced by these companies. Also popular was the Rodian [[Stalker Armor M1-10|Stalker armor]] and [[Cam droid/Legends|Rodian hovercam]].

[[File:DarWac-SWCTP.png|thumb|right|180px|[[Dar Wac/Legends|Dar Wac]], a Rodian aide to Chancellor Palpatine.]]
Rodians also became involved in many other forms of criminal activities. Some became very successful in this underworld, such as the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Vigo/Legends|Vigos]] [[Dardo]] and [[Clezo]]. Others, such as [[Reelo Baruk]]<ref name="JO" /> and [[Ne'Chak]], went out on their own, establishing their own criminal organizations, often employing many Rodians, as well as other species, as lackeys. Rodians worked for the criminal organizations like the [[Exchange]], the [[Sabiador Slavers]], or as pirates such as [[Lekk Bazak]]. Other notorious Rodian criminals included [[Slerog Fenn]], [[Ten-Suckers Madoom]] and the terrorists [[Beekly Grimlok]] and [[Lorgal]]. Many Rodians also frequently worked in gray areas, such as the smugglers [[Chihdo/Legends|Chihdo]] and [[Chordak]].

===Legitimacy===
Despite this proclivity towards crime, many Rodians found fulfillment in more legitimate professions. Rodians were apt mechanics, commonly working among [[Podracer/Legends|podracers]], while a number became successful musicians, such as [[Doda Bodonawieedo/Legends|Doda Bodonawieedo]] and [[Greeata Jendowanian/Legends|Greeata Jendowanian]]. Others still became successful businessmen, such as [[Kelko]], the owner of [[Shusko Station]] mining operation. Another well-known Rodian was treasure hunter and archaeologist [[Suz Tanwa]], who discovered many precious items from her ancestor [[Suvam Tan]].

Many Rodians also joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in various capacities. The elite fighter squadron [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] contained a number of Rodian pilots such as [[Koobis Nu]], [[Andoorni Hui]], and [[Standro Jcir]]. Many others fought in various other capacities, such as [[Oepoono]] and [[Othik Wespoch]]&mdash;both members of the [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance Special Forces]].

Rodians went on to work in high positions in the New Republic, such as the [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] Navik the Red (who was also a member of the [[New Republic Advisory Council]], under the name "Narik") and [[Moog Ulur]].

===Force-sensitives===
[[File:MahteeWeeDunn-TCWCE.png|thumb|left|150px|Force-sensitive Wee Dunn and his mother]]
During the Old Republic, [[Dree Vandap]] fought in the [[New Sith Wars]], and a [[Unidentified Rodian Jedi (Yinchorri Uprising)|Rodian Jedi]] fought in the [[Yinchorri/Legends|Yinchorri]] [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|raid]] on the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], and the [[First Battle of Kamino]]. The Rodian [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Bolla Ropal/Legends|Bolla Ropal]] was part of the Jedi Order during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], until he was tortured to death at the hands of bounty hunter [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]]. Bane later kidnapped Force-sensitive infants for [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. Among them was the Rodian [[Wee Dunn/Legends|Wee Dunn]], who was taken from his mother, [[Mahtee Dunn/Legends|Mahtee]].

In the New Jedi Order, [[Kelbis Nu]], [[Jovan Drark]], [[Toile Senn]] and [[Twool (Rodian)|Twool]] were all trained Jedi Knights. Both Nu and Drark were killed during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]; Nu on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] and Drark on the successful but costly [[mission to Myrkr]]. Senn was later killed in the [[Battle of Tralus (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Tralus]] of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. Twool perished months later during the [[Battle of Centerpoint Station (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Centerpoint Station]] during an engagement with [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]].

[[Unidentified Rodian Sith|A Rodian]] was also known to be part of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith|Sith Order]], part of the team that ambushed Jedi on the planet [[Daluuj/Legends|Daluuj]] in [[137 ABY]].

Some Rodians, such as [[Vinto]], had close associations with Jedi, often working with them on various missions, while others, such as [[Paemos]], were not allied with any particular Force tradition but knew and taught some tricks nevertheless.
There were also a number of Rodians in [[Bartyn's Landing]], the capital town of [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]], c. [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]].<ref name="R">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Rodians in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] were referred to during production as [[Wikipedia:Martian|Martians]], and in [[1978]] were identified in a memo as "Graffties," a reference to the [[George Lucas]] film ''American Graffiti''. The Rodian costume used for [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] was fixed up differently with two extra arms and used for [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]], who at the time was referred to as a "Plutonian."

In the original versions of ''A New Hope'' and ''Return of the Jedi'', all the Rodian background characters wore the same costume as Greedo. The Rodians added to the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] in the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] of ''Return of the Jedi'' were the first Rodians to have their own costumes, not to mention the first Rodians to appear on screen who were not bounty hunters.

The name "Rodian" first appeared in ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'', but was later used in scripts and production notes for the [[prequel trilogy]]. This makes it one of the few [[List of Legends elements in the films|elements that originated in ''Star Wars'' Legends to appear in the films]].
